proof:
# Zero parity-forest slack does not bound the centroid-graph Helly number

There are actual full-dimensional convex bodies with two integer
coordinates and any continuous dimension d>=1 for which every edge of
the volume-maximal parity forest is an exact Minkowski equality, with
unique parity maxima, but the finite centroid graph has Helly number
at least five. There are only four occupied parity classes.

Thus the proposed conclusion h(centroid graph)<=2^n is false even
under the exact equality model. This is not a counterexample to OC.
In a particular d=2 instance below no fiber alone has a quarter of
the total mass, yet an explicit different counting argument proves
the OC bound at a graph point.

## 1. An actual concave homothetic family

Use the following eight integer bases, with the displayed integer
height t_i:

| i | p_i | t_i |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | (-1,-2) | 8 |
| 1 | (-1,-1) | 11 |
| 2 | (-1,0) | 14 |
| 3 | (0,0) | 16 |
| 4 | (0,1) | 12 |
| 5 | (0,2) | 8 |
| 6 | (1,2) | 10 |
| 7 | (2,3) | 8 |

Their convex hull Q is the quadrilateral with vertices p_0,p_2,p_5,p_7.
Its exact inequalities are

    -2 z1+z2<=2,   -z1<=1,   -z1+2 z2<=4,
    5 z1-3 z2<=1.                                      (1)

The integer points of Q are exactly the eight listed bases. This can
be checked in the bounding box [-1,2] times [-2,3], or directly from
the upper and lower bounds on z2 in (1).

Define on Q the concave piecewise-affine function

    t(z)=min{16+2 z1+3 z2,
             16+2 z1-4 z2,
             16-40 z1+24 z2}.                          (2)

At the eight bases it takes precisely the tabulated values. Its
minimum is eight: it is concave, and its values at all four vertices
of Q are at least eight. Fix any R>=0 and put

    r(z)=R+t(z)/8.

For the standard d-simplex

    K={x in R^d:x_j>=0, sum_j x_j<=1},

let

    C_R={ (z,x):z in Q, x_j>=0, sum_j x_j<=r(z)}.         (3)

Equations (1)--(3) are a finite system of affine inequalities: the
last inequality in (3) is imposed for each of the three affine
functions in (2). Hence C_R is an actual compact convex polytope.
It is full-dimensional since Q has interior and r is strictly
positive. Its actual integer fibers are exactly

    K_i=r_i K,       r_i=R+t_i/8,
    |K_i|=r_i^d/d!,
    g_i=r_i (1,...,1)/(d+1).                            (4)

If an exact hull-of-the-mixed-source convention is desired, replace
C_R by the convex hull of the eight lifted full fibers. It remains
full-dimensional and contained in C_R; it includes every full
integer fiber in (4), so all those fibers are unchanged. Projection
onto Q supplies no additional integer bases. Thus every assertion
below also holds for an actual body equal to the hull of its mixed
source.

## 2. Every prescribed forest edge is an exact equality

The unique parity-volume maxima are

    v_(1,0)=p_2,  v_(1,1)=p_1,
    v_(0,0)=p_3,  v_(0,1)=p_4.                         (5)

Uniqueness follows from the tabulated heights, for every d>=1 and
R>=0. In particular the minimum-norm tie convention has no role.
The four nonroot forest edges z -> (z+v_[z])/2 are

    p_0 -> p_1,   partner p_2;
    p_5 -> p_4,   partner p_3;
    p_6 -> p_4,   partner p_2;
    p_7 -> p_6,   partner p_4.                         (6)

The height equalities are, respectively,

    2*11=8+14,    2*12=8+16,
    2*12=10+14,   2*10=8+12.                         (7)

Adding the same R to every radius preserves these equalities.
Consequently every forest edge has the exact set identity

    K_(F(z))=(K_z+K_(v_[z]))/2,                        (8)

not merely equality of volume roots. The radius and centroid
identities both hold on every edge. All fibers even share one
common simplex shape. The forest has four roots and no unresolved
cycle or tie.

## 3. An exact five-point graph Helly obstruction

The centroid graph in (4) is affinely isomorphic to the eight points

    G_i=(p_i,t_i) in R^3.                              (9)

Indeed on its affine hull use the map
(z,x) -> (z,8(d+1)x_1-8R). Consider the subset

    W={G_0,G_1,G_3,G_4,G_6}.                           (10)

Each is a vertex of conv(W). In the order (0,1,3,4,6), strictly
exposing normals and their minimum positive gaps against the
other four points are

| i | exposing normal | minimum gap |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | (-5,-1,0) | 1 |
| 1 | (-16,4,1) | 7 |
| 3 | (-11,4,3) | 8 |
| 4 | (-16,11,1) | 7 |
| 6 | (-5,6,0) | 1 |

There are no further graph points in conv(W). The three inequalities

    -9 z1+4 z2+t <=16,
    -5 z1+3 z2-t <=-9,
    2 z1-z2 <=0                                      (11)

all hold on W. The omitted points G_2,G_5,G_7 violate, respectively,
these inequalities by the strictly positive amounts 7,7,1. Thus

    conv(W) intersect {G_0,...,G_7}=W.                 (12)

For each i in {0,1,3,4,6}, let H_i=conv(W minus {G_i}).
Every four of these five convex sets contain the graph point whose
index was omitted from the family. Their full intersection contains
no graph point: by (12) any possible point is in W, while G_i is
not in H_i because it is a vertex. This is a direct five-set Helly
witness for the finite graph, proving

    h({(p_i,g_i):0<=i<=7})>=5>4=2^2.                  (13)

No general characterization of finite-set Helly numbers is needed.
In particular the calculation does not infer a Helly number from
the dimension of the linear space of forest identities.

The missing full Jensen identity can also be seen directly:

    p_3=(1/2)p_0+(1/6)p_2+(1/3)p_7,
    t_3=16 > (1/2)t_0+(1/6)t_2+(1/3)t_7=9.            (13a)

Thus even the hull of the full centroid graph has a non-singleton
section at this integer base, despite all the exact forest-edge
identities. This is a genuine untested anchored relation.

## 4. A non-heavy instance which nevertheless satisfies OC

For d=2 and R=1, express the eight fiber areas in units |K|/64.
They are

    (256,361,484,576,400,256,324,256),
    total=2913.                                       (14)

The heaviest fiber is strictly less than a quarter of the total,
since 4*576<2913. Therefore this instance is not settled just by
the largest original fiber.

It still satisfies OC at the actual point (p_4,g_4). The exact
graph relations from (6) give the two DISJOINT pairs

    (G_3+G_5)/2=G_4,    (G_2+G_6)/2=G_4.

Every containing ambient halfspace contains G_4 and at least one
centroid from each pair. Ordinary Grunbaum in these three distinct
fibers therefore gives original normalized depth at least

    Gamma_2 [400+min(576,256)+min(484,324)]/2913
       = Gamma_2*980/2913 > Gamma_2/4.                 (15)

Whole-fiber restrictions only improve the bound. This separates
the failed graph-Helly implication from the still viable weighted
depth problem in the equality model. The note neither proves nor
refutes OC for every zero-slack forest family.

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_zero_forest_centroid_graph_obstruction.py` gives a standalone
standard-library rational certificate for the actual profile,
lattice bases, unique roots, edge equalities, five-point witness,
and the exact non-heavy instance (14)--(15). The preliminary LP
search is not a proof dependency.
